_about: Labeled regression smoke set for the DETERMINISTIC injection-defense layers (Layer 1 static patterns in security/prompt_guard.py + Layer 2 normalization/decoding in security/injection_defense.py). Malicious cases are NOT duplicated here: they reference the shared adversarial corpus by category/index via the `source` field (corpus: = hand-crafted tests/adversarial_payloads.py; corpus_open: = vendored CC-BY-4.0 subset tests/adversarial_payloads_open.py), so there is one payload source, not copies. Benign look-alikes carry literal `input` text to measure false positives; the benign_encoded category measures the false-positive surface of the Layer 2 decoding pass on legitimate encoded content (data URIs, JWTs, hex digests, base64 blobs) as seen on the MCP/remote-agent surfaces, which run advanced=True. The open_* categories are baselined at MEASURED values: open_injection (subtle English framings) and open_multilingual (non-English) carry expected=flag but at baseline time ALL of them PASSED the English-centric pattern layers (14/14 and 18/18) -> measured false negatives that are the LLM-backed Layer 3 screen's job (multilingual efficacy UNMEASURED); open_content_safety carry expected=pass so any Layer-1 trip is a measured false positive. This is NOT a security benchmark and does NOT cover Layer 3 (the Sentinel semantic screen, which needs an LLM). See evals/README.md and docs/SECURITY_MAPPING.md.

label_semantics.block: expected to be caught by Layer 1 static patterns (detect_injection_attempt without advanced)
label_semantics.flag: expected to be caught only after Layer 2 (unicode/encoding normalization, invisible-char stripping, fence neutralization, or multi-turn poisoning detection)
label_semantics.pass: benign: expected to be neither blocked nor flagged
